title: File Uploads
summary: Handle file uploads with UploadFile, validate content types and sizes, and stream safely.

sections.content: Use UploadFile for file uploads. It gives you filename, content_type, and async read/seek/write methods. The file is stored as a SpooledTemporaryFile (in memory until ~1MB, then on disk).
Alternatively, for small files you can use bytes with File():

sections.title: Never trust file.filename
sections.content: File names can contain path traversal (../) or dangerous characters. Always generate your own filenames (e.g., uuid4) and validate content type AND size.

sections.title: Streaming upload best practices
sections.content: 1) Never trust file.filename — generate your own. 2) Validate content type and size. 3) Stream writes in chunks, don't load the whole file in memory. 4) Check size during streaming, not just at the end.

code_challenge.title: File Upload with Validation
code_challenge.description: Create POST /upload that accepts an UploadFile, returns filename and content_type. Reject non-image files with 415.
hints: Raise HTTPException(415, 'Unsupported file type') if not allowed
TestClient without a file will get 422 (missing required field)
code_challenge.note: The TestClient request without a file body tests that the endpoint requires a file (422). Full file upload testing requires multipart form data.

quiz.question: What does UploadFile provide that bytes (File()) does not?
quiz.explanation: UploadFile gives you file.filename, file.content_type, and async streaming methods (read, seek, write). bytes loads everything in memory at once.

quiz.question: Why should you never use file.filename directly for saving?
options: It can contain path traversal (../) or dangerous characters
quiz.explanation: file.filename can contain path traversal attacks or dangerous characters. Always generate your own filename (e.g., uuid4) for storage.

quiz.question: How should you handle large file uploads?
options: Read all at once with file.read()
quiz.explanation: Stream in chunks using await file.read(chunk_size). This avoids loading the entire file into memory.

quiz.question: What status code should you return for an unsupported file type?
quiz.explanation: 415 Unsupported Media Type is the appropriate status code when the file content type is not allowed.

quiz.question: Where does UploadFile store the file data initially?
quiz.explanation: UploadFile uses SpooledTemporaryFile — data stays in memory until ~1MB, then spills to disk. This balances speed and memory usage.
